data.title: A hut that grew into a lodge.
data.intro: Pinecrest is a seven-bed lodge on Larch Ridge, run by the same family for three generations.

children.text: How it started
Pinecrest began in 1958 as a one-room hut that the Haldane family built for hunting season. They added a kitchen, then a second floor, and by the 1970s were taking in walkers for the summer.
Ingrid Haldane took over in 2016. The lodge was cold in winter and the roof leaked at the north corner, so the first two years went on insulation, a new slate roof and a wood range for the kitchen.
The lodge today
There are four rooms in the main lodge and three cabins on the ridge path. The lodge has a lounge with a stone fireplace, a dining room, a deck with a fire pit and a cedar sauna.
Most of what you see is local: the stone is from the quarry below Brookmere, the pine panelling was milled in the valley and the wool blankets are woven by a family two valleys over.
Staying small
We have never wanted more than seven places to sleep. It means the same people cook your breakfast, light your fire and remember how you take your coffee.

data.title: Lodge policies
data.intro: The short version of how a stay works. Please read it before you send a request.

children.text: Check-in and check-out
Check-in is from 3:00 pm and check-out is by 10:30 am. If you will arrive after 8:00 pm, tell us when you request your dates and we will leave a key and a lamp lit.
Cancellation

This is sample text for the theme. Edit it to match your own terms. For example: free cancellation up to 14 days before arrival, half the first night charged from 14 to 3 days, and the first night charged after that.
Children and pets
Children are welcome in every room and cabin. Dogs are welcome in Juniper, Heron and Timber cabins for a $25 cleaning charge per stay. Please keep dogs off the beds and on a lead near the lodge.
Fires and quiet
The deck fire pits and the cabin fire bowls can be used until 10:00 pm. Quiet hours run from 10:00 pm to 7:00 am. We are a long way from the nearest neighbour, but sound carries across the valley.
Smoking
No smoking inside the lodge or the cabins. There is a covered spot by the car park with a bucket of sand.
Winter driving
From 1 November to 15 April you must carry winter tyres or chains. If you would rather not drive the last 11 km, ask us and we will collect you from Brookmere.

data.title: Spruce Room
data.summary: A double room on the first floor of the lodge with a wide window onto the valley and a plaid wool blanket on the bed.
data.amenities:
Window seat facing the valley
Private bathroom with a walk-in shower
Wool blankets and a second set of pillows
Kettle, tea and ground coffee
Underfloor heating in the bathroom
data.intro: The quietest room on the upper floor, with a window seat for watching the light change on the peaks.

children.text: About the room

The Spruce Room is at the end of the first-floor corridor, so there is no foot traffic outside the door. The bed faces the window and the valley below, and the window seat is wide enough to sit with a book and a cup of tea.
The walls and ceiling are pine, left unpainted. The bathroom has a walk-in shower and a heated floor, which is welcome after a day on the trail.

data.photo_alt: A queen bed with a plaid wool blanket beside a tall window that looks onto snow-capped peaks

data.title: Larch Room
data.summary: A king room with a reading lamp on each side of the bed and a small balcony facing the peaks.
data.amenities:
Balcony with two chairs
Private bathroom with a bath
Reading lamp on both sides of the bed
Kettle, tea and ground coffee
Blackout curtains
data.intro: A king room with a balcony that catches the first sun on the high peaks.

children.text: About the room
The Larch Room faces east. In summer the sun is on the balcony by six, and in winter it reaches the peaks first and the balcony an hour later.
There is a bath as well as a shower, and the bed has a wool throw in a brown plaid. Blackout curtains keep the room dark if you want to sleep past the sunrise.

data.photo_alt: A bed with a plaid blanket, a wall lamp and a vase of greenery, with a window onto the mountains

data.title: Alder Family Room
data.summary: A two-room family unit with a queen bed, two bunks and space to spread out when the weather turns.
data.amenities:
Separate sleeping area with two bunks
Private bathroom with a bath
Table for four
Board games and a shelf of paperbacks
Travel cot on request, no charge
data.intro: Two rooms joined by a short passage, one for parents and one for children.

children.text: About the room
The Alder Family Room has a queen bed in the main room and a small bunk room next to it, joined by an open doorway with a curtain. The table in the main room seats four for card games or puzzles.
Children are welcome in all rooms and cabins. A travel cot, a high chair and a step stool for the bathroom basin are free if you ask when you book.

data.photo_alt: A bed with a plaid wool blanket and white pillows in a timber room

data.title: Ridge Suite
data.summary: The largest room in the lodge, with a corner window, a wood fireplace and a sitting area facing the peaks.
data.amenities:
Wood fireplace, logs and kindling supplied
Corner window and sitting area
Private bathroom with a bath and a shower
Kettle, tea and ground coffee
Underfloor heating throughout
data.intro: A corner room with a fireplace and the widest view in the lodge.

children.text: About the suite
The Ridge Suite takes the whole corner of the first floor. One window faces the peaks and the other the valley, and an armchair sits where you can see both.
We lay the fire before you arrive in the colder months. Logs and kindling are in the basket by the hearth, and the lodge team will bring more if you run low.

data.photo_alt: A tall window framing a range of snowy peaks above a bed and an upholstered armchair

data.title: Juniper Cabin
data.summary: A one-bedroom cabin on the ridge path with a wood stove, a small kitchen and a porch facing the sunset.
data.beds: 1 king bed and a sofa bed
data.amenities:
Wood stove, logs supplied
Small kitchen with a two-ring hob
Porch with two chairs
Private bathroom with a walk-in shower
Breakfast delivered to the door on request
data.intro: A cabin for two or four, 150 steps from the lodge on a gravel path.

children.text: About the cabin
Juniper Cabin sits on the ridge path about 150 steps from the lodge. It has one bedroom, a living area with a sofa bed and a wood stove, and a small kitchen for making tea and breakfast.
The porch faces west, so evenings here are long and orange. The cabin has no Wi-Fi, but the lodge lounge is a short walk up the path.

data.photo_alt: A timber deck with an armchair and a lantern in front of glowing lodge windows

data.title: Heron Cabin
data.summary: A small cabin for two with a wood stove, a deep tub and a deck above the river bend.
data.amenities:
Wood stove, logs supplied
Deep soaking tub
Deck with a fire bowl and two chairs
Kettle, tea and ground coffee
Private parking beside the door
data.intro: A cabin for two, set apart from the others at the end of the path.

children.text: About the cabin
Heron Cabin is the last on the path and the furthest from the lodge, about five minutes on foot. The deck looks down on a bend in the river, and on still mornings the valley fills with low cloud.
There is a deep tub in the bathroom and a wood stove in the main room. The fire bowl on the deck can be used until 10 pm.

data.photo_alt: A stone fire pit burning on a timber deck beside wooden chairs, with a lit glass-fronted lodge behind

data.title: Timber Cabin
data.summary: A three-bedroom cabin for up to six, with a long table, a stone fireplace and a glass front facing the peaks.
data.beds: 1 king bed, 1 queen bed and 2 singles
data.amenities:
Stone fireplace, logs supplied
Full kitchen with an oven
Long table that seats eight
Two bathrooms
Deck with a fire pit
data.intro: Three bedrooms, a full kitchen and a long table for family weekends or small groups.

children.text: About the cabin
Timber Cabin has a glass front that looks straight at the peaks. The main room has a stone fireplace, a long table and a full kitchen, so a group can cook and eat together.
It has three bedrooms and two bathrooms. Dinner from the lodge kitchen can be sent down on request, with a day's notice.

data.photo_alt: A timber and stone cabin with a steep roof and a stone chimney under a dusk sky

data.title: Day hikes
data.summary: Marked trails start at the lodge door. Short loops to the lower tarn take two hours and the ridge walk to Cairn Point takes most of a day.
data.bring:
Sturdy boots
1.5 litres of water each
Rain jacket
Sun hat and sun cream
Paper map (we lend one)
data.details:
Best months|June to September
Starts|From the lodge door
Guide|Tomas leads a group walk on Wednesdays at 9:00 am, no charge
data.photo_alt: A snow-capped mountain range above low cloud at sunrise

data.title: Snowshoeing
data.summary: Snowshoes and poles are lent to guests. The loop through the larch wood is flat and takes about two hours. The trail to the viewpoint climbs for the last half hour.
data.bring:
Warm layers and a hat
Waterproof gloves
Sunglasses
Boots with room for thick socks
Thermos (we fill it)
data.details:
Best months|December to March
Hire|Snowshoes and poles free for guests
Guide|Tomas leads a group on Saturdays at 10:00 am
data.photo_alt: Tall pines on a ridge above a misty valley

data.title: Wood-fired sauna
data.summary: A cedar sauna beside the lodge, heated by wood from late afternoon. Slots are for one party of up to six, so you have it to yourselves.
data.bring:
Towel (we lend one for a small fee)
Sandals
Water bottle
data.details:
Open|Daily from 4:00 pm
Price|$30 per slot, up to six people
Book|At the front desk by noon
data.photo_alt: Warm lights glowing inside a timber and glass lodge at dusk

data.title: Stargazing on the deck
data.summary: On clear nights the sky over the ridge is dark enough to see the Milky Way. We keep the deck lights off, put out blankets and leave a thermos of hot chocolate.
data.bring:
Warm hat
Gloves
Something to sit on (we lend blankets)
data.details:
Best months|September to March
Where|The lodge deck, lights off
Cancelled|If the cloud is down, no charge
data.photo_alt: A sun low over mountain ridges and a pink-orange sky

data.title: Lake swim
data.summary: The lower tarn is a 35-minute walk and stays cold into July. Most guests swim for a few minutes, then sit on the rocks to dry off.
data.bring:
Towel
Water shoes
Snack
Sun cream
data.details:
Best months|July to early September
Water|Cold, around 14 degrees C
No lifeguard|Swim at your own risk
data.photo_alt: Mist lying over a mountain lake at sunrise

data.title: Cross-country skiing
data.summary: Nine kilometres of groomed track run through the forest below the lodge. Skis can be hired in Brookmere, and we can book them for you.
data.bring:
Warm layers
Light gloves
Sunglasses
Snack
data.details:
Best months|January to early March
Trail|9 km groomed, two loops
Hire|In Brookmere, from $22 a day
data.photo_alt: A timber lodge with tall glass windows lit at dusk

data.title: Kitchen and breakfast
data.summary: Breakfast is included with every stay. Dinner is a set menu on four nights, cooked on a wood range and served at one long table.
data.bring: Tell us about allergies when you request your dates
data.details:
Breakfast|7:30 to 10:00 am, every day
Dinner|Thursday to Sunday, 6:30 pm
Packed lunch|$12, ask the evening before

data.title: Ingrid
data.bio: Ingrid took over the lodge from her parents in 2016 and lives in the cottage below the car park. She is at the front desk most mornings.

data.title: Rafe
data.bio: Rafe cooks breakfast and the Thursday to Sunday dinners on the wood range. He bakes the bread the night before.

data.title: Mina
data.bio: Mina answers the phone and the booking emails. She can tell you which cabin is warmest in January.

data.title: Tomas
data.bio: Tomas has walked the ridge trails for twenty years and leads the Wednesday and Saturday group outings.

data.title: Dale
data.bio: Dale clears the road, stacks the firewood and drives guests up from Brookmere when the snow is deep.

data.parking: Free for every guest, eight spaces by the lodge and six by the cabins
data.road: From the village of Brookmere take Larch Ridge Road for 11 km. The last 3 km are gravel and take about 15 minutes. There is no phone signal on the upper road, so save these directions before you set off.
data.winter_note: From 1 November to 15 April you must carry winter tyres or chains. Dale can collect you from Brookmere if you would rather not drive the last 11 km.
data.request_note: This form sends a request by email. It is not a booking. We reply within a day to confirm availability and the rate, and nothing is charged until you agree.
